companies.name: Loblaw Companies
companies.banners: Loblaws, No Frills, Real Canadian Superstore, Shoppers Drug Mart, T&T
notes: Roughly 70% of sales are food and 30% drug (Shoppers Drug Mart).
Most grocery stores are franchised, so headcount and store economics are not directly comparable with corporate-run chains.

stores.basis: Grocery + Shoppers Drug Mart, incl. franchised/associate-owned

loyalty.evidence: PC Optimum, one of Canada's largest loyalty programs

fin.evidence: Sold PC Financial to EQB; received $625M after Q2 2026; now books its share of EQB income

digital.evidence: E-commerce sales +19.3% in Q2 2026 (PC Express + third-party delivery)

health.evidence: Pharmacy & healthcare services same-store sales +7.5% in Q2 2026

private.evidence: President's Choice and No Name house brands

franchise.evidence: Most grocery stores run by franchisees; Shoppers by associate-owners

log.action: Opened 14 stores in Q2, including 7 hard-discount and 3 drug stores
Closed sale of PC Financial to EQB
About $2.1B of share buybacks planned for 2026
Raised the number of new stores planned for 2026

actions: Keep shifting the mix to hard discount and pharmacy services, the two lines growing fastest while conventional grocery comps slow to 1.6%.
Monetize the PC Optimum data asset through Loblaw Advance now that PC Financial is gone, to replace that lost profit stream.
Hold the $2.1B buyback pace only while free cash flow (C$5.3B TTM) stays above 2.5× capex.

companies.name: Alimentation Couche-Tard
notes: Reports in US dollars; converted to CAD at the Oct 9, 2026 close.
Revenue includes road-transportation fuel, so margins and revenue per store sit on a different scale from merchandise retailers.
Only a small share of its stores are in Canada.

fuel.evidence: Road-transportation fuel across North America and Europe; U.S. margin 52.6¢/gal in Q1 FY2027

intl.evidence: Stores in North America, Europe and Asia; licensed Circle K in other markets

acq.evidence: Agreed to buy a controlling stake in Żabka Group (Poland), closing expected by end of 2026

food.evidence: Foodservice push: meal-deal bundles ~14M in Q1, U.S. hot food +11%

private.evidence: Circle K private-label beverages and snacks

log.action: 26 sites added in Q1; about 42 under construction
log.impact: More than 100 openings planned for FY2027

log.action: Long-term plan for 750 new stores by 2030
Controlling stake in Żabka Group agreed
log.impact: Leverage to rise above 2–2.5× at closing

log.action: Normalized expenses up 2.7%, below weighted inflation

actions: Integrate Żabka quickly: it is what lifts consensus revenue 14% this year, and the year after is forecast to slip 1.2%.
Scale foodservice, the highest-margin merchandise line, to cushion any normalization in fuel margins.
Rebuild leverage toward 2× before restarting buybacks.

companies.name: Empire Company (Sobeys)
companies.banners: Sobeys, Safeway, IGA, FreshCo, Foodland, Farm Boy, Voilà
notes: Trailing net income ($219M) is far below its own 5-year run-rate of about $700M a year, which inflates the P/E.
The company's own factsheet gives FY2026 sales of $31.95B; the data source's $32.03B includes other revenue.

digital.evidence: Voilà e-commerce under review; combined e-commerce sales +11.3% in Q1 FY2027

health.evidence: Buying nine Morelli's pharmacies to convert to Longo's Pharmacy

acq.evidence: Completed Mayrand Food Group acquisition in Q1 FY2027

franchise.evidence: Franchise and affiliate stores across banners

log.action: First two FreshCo discount stores opened in Atlantic Canada
Renovate 20–25% of the store network between FY2027 and FY2029
log.impact: FY2027 capex ~$850M, about half for renovations and new stores

log.action: E-commerce (Voilà) review
Mayrand Food Group acquisition completed

actions: Land the $95M Voilà fix first; it is worth more than a third of trailing net income.
Pace FreshCo openings in the East, where discount demand is outgrowing conventional banners.
Use the 20–25% renovation program to raise sales per store; at 0.34× sales the market is pricing in no improvement.

companies.name: Metro Inc.
companies.banners: Metro, Super C, Food Basics, Adonis, Jean Coutu, Brunet
notes: Employee figure counts people employed directly or indirectly, including franchised and affiliated stores.

health.evidence: Jean Coutu and Brunet pharmacies; pharmacy same-store sales +4.8% in Q3 2026

digital.evidence: Online food sales +16.3% in Q3 2026; delivery moving to the store network

franchise.evidence: Franchised Jean Coutu pharmacies and affiliated grocers

log.action: Converting 10 Ontario Metro stores to Food Basics; closing 1 store, a satellite warehouse and the Montréal e-commerce fulfilment centre
log.impact: ~$15M recurring annual net earnings by FY2028; $42.6M after-tax charges

log.action: Discount acceleration plan: about a dozen new or converted stores this year
Laval distribution-centre labour conflict
log.impact: $66M after-tax hit in Q3; Q4 also affected

actions: Resolve the Laval labour conflict: its $66M after-tax cost in one quarter outweighs four years of the restructuring savings.
Keep converting weak conventional stores to Food Basics; food same-store sales fell 1.5% while pharmacy grew 4.8%.
Lean on Jean Coutu health services, the steadiest growth line.

companies.name: Canadian Tire Corporation
companies.banners: Canadian Tire, SportChek, Mark's, Party City, Gas+, Canadian Tire Bank
notes: Debt includes funding for Canadian Tire Bank's credit-card receivables, so leverage ratios overstate retail-only debt.
Headcount excludes staff employed by independent Canadian Tire dealers.

stores.basis: All retail banners incl. Gas+, dealer-operated

loyalty.evidence: Triangle Rewards: 2M+ members active with partners incl. Petro-Canada, RBC, WestJet; Tims Rewards link coming

fin.evidence: Canadian Tire Bank credit cards; receivables +4.2%

private.evidence: Owned Brands such as Mastercraft, NOMA and Woods

franchise.evidence: Independent Canadian Tire dealers run the stores

data.evidence: DaiVID AI pricing tool cut regular prices on 5,000+ items

log.action: 30 store refreshes done in H1; more than double by year-end
2026 capital spending narrowed to C$450–500M
Retail SG&A down C$10M year over year
Regular prices cut on 5,000+ products using AI pricing

actions: Grow Triangle partnerships into a paid data and media business; the loyalty base is a bigger asset than the store count.
Watch the bank: net write-offs near 7.2% mean credit losses can erase retail gains in a downturn.
Finish the store-refresh program before adding capex; revenue barely moved over four years (0.04% CAGR).

companies.name: Dollarama
companies.banners: Dollarama, The Reject Shop (Australia), 60% of Dollarcity (Latin America)
notes: Part of the recent growth comes from adding The Reject Shop's Australian stores; Canadian comparable sales grew 5.4% in Q2.
ROE above 90% reflects heavy share buybacks shrinking equity, so this dashboard ranks returns on ROIC instead.

stores.basis: 1,734 in Canada + 414 Reject Shop (Australia); excludes 781 Dollarcity

intl.evidence: The Reject Shop (Australia, 414 stores) and Dollarcity (Latin America, now in Mexico)

acq.evidence: Acquired The Reject Shop; 60.1% of Dollarcity

private.evidence: Mostly direct-sourced, own-label goods at fixed price points

log.action: FY2027 target raised to 65–75 net new Canadian stores
Western Canada logistics hub under construction
Australia: 38 stores renovated so far this year; 60 of 414 on Dollarama layouts
Dollarcity Mexico rollout accelerated after Guadalajara launch

actions: Prove the Australian model before speeding up: Reject Shop conversions will weigh on H2 sales.
Hold the $5 price ceiling as long as possible; it's the core of the traffic story.
Growth is forecast to halve to 6.6% next year, so Mexico and Australia need to carry more of it.

companies.name: lululemon athletica
notes: Listed in New York and reports in US dollars; converted to CAD at the Oct 9, 2026 close.
Q2 comparable sales fell 9% and Canada revenue fell 11%; the share price sits near its 52-week low.
Lululemon calls the year ended Feb 1, 2026 'fiscal 2025'. This dashboard labels years by their end date to avoid that trap.
companies.guidance: Company outlook: FY revenue US$10.35–10.50B, a 5–7% decline

intl.evidence: International revenue +4% in Q2; China Mainland −2% in constant dollars

log.action: 35 net new stores planned for 2026, cut from ~40; ~25 international
New CEO Heidi O'Neill joining
2.7M shares repurchased in Q2

actions: Fix the Americas first: comps fell 12% there, and both forecast years show shrinking revenue.
Slow store openings further until traffic and conversion recover; protect the 23.7% ROIC.
Rebuild product newness and marketing, the levers management itself named.

companies.name: Aritzia
companies.banners: Aritzia, Babaton, Wilfred, TNA, Super Puff
notes: Digital sales were 29.9% of Q1 revenue, which lifts revenue per boutique.
Q1 comparable sales grew 35.1%, the fastest of any company here.

intl.evidence: U.S. now 67.1% of revenue; 76 U.S. vs 67 Canadian boutiques

private.evidence: Own exclusive brands: Babaton, Wilfred, TNA, Super Puff

log.action: 380,000 sq ft British Columbia distribution centre went live
log.impact: Next major DC planned for the U.S.

log.action: 12–13 new boutiques in FY2027, 11–12 in the U.S.
About $250M capital spending in FY2027
log.impact: New boutiques pay back in under a year on average

log.action: Four-level ~42,000 sq ft flagship at CF Pacific Centre

actions: Keep opening U.S. boutiques at the current pace; payback under a year is the best capital return in this group.
Build the U.S. distribution centre before the store pipeline outruns logistics.
Plan for growth to slow from 27% to 15% next year as the comparison base gets harder.

companies.name: Canada Goose
notes: Highly seasonal: most revenue and nearly all profit land in the October–December quarter.
Revenue per store is inflated because a large share of sales is wholesale and e-commerce, not stores.

intl.evidence: Asia Pacific is a main source of DTC growth

digital.evidence: E-commerce up double digits in Q1 FY2027

private.evidence: Single own brand; expanding into rainwear, windwear and apparel

log.action: Four net new stores in Q1; 92 directly operated
SG&A down to $178.0M from $224.9M
Scope 1 and 2 emissions down 50% vs fiscal 2019

actions: Push year-round categories harder; one quarter still earns nearly all the profit.
Grow wholesale selectively to fill off-season capacity rather than opening more stores while DTC comps are negative.
Inventory turns only once a year; cut SKUs before adding categories.

companies.name: Pet Valu
companies.banners: Pet Valu, Bosley's, Tisol, Total Pet, Chico
notes: Most stores are franchised, which is why 877 stores run on about 2,200 employees and revenue per employee looks high.
Same-store sales slipped 0.2% in Q2 2026; the stock is down about half from its 52-week high.
companies.guidance: Company outlook: revenue +2% to +4% on a comparable-week basis; adjusted EBITDA margin about 21%

franchise.evidence: About 71% of 877 stores franchised; sold 11 corporate stores to franchisees in Q2

digital.evidence: Record digital growth from Click & Collect, delivery and AutoShip

private.evidence: Own brands across food and supplies

log.action: 7 stores opened in Q2, 15 in H1; 877 total
11 corporate stores sold to franchisees
DC labour-management systems and training

actions: Use the 90%-of-sales loyalty base to sell subscriptions (AutoShip) and services, not just product.
Prioritize the rural and Quebec white space behind the 1,200-store target.
At 3.9× net debt to EBITDA, keep franchise-resale gains going to debt rather than buybacks.

companies.name: Leon's Furniture (LFL Group)
companies.banners: Leon's, The Brick, Brick Outlet, The Brick Mattress Store
notes: The 11.8% trailing yield includes a special dividend. The regular $0.24 quarterly dividend works out to about 3.8%.
The data source's EBITDA is below its operating income, so EV/EBITDA and leverage are left blank rather than shown wrong.

fin.evidence: Retail financing fees (falling with lower Bank of Canada rates)

services.evidence: Insurance, warranty and delivery revenue rose in Q2 2026

franchise.evidence: Corporate and franchise stores; 4 franchise openings in Q2 2026

digital.evidence: E-commerce named as a growth investment

log.action: Four new franchise locations opened
SG&A rose to 36.85% of revenue
Liquidity rose to $560.1M

actions: Put the $560M of liquidity to work on e-commerce and fulfilment; revenue is forecast to shrink 0.9% this year.
Push insurance, warranty and delivery services to offset lower financing fees.
Bring SG&A back under 36% of revenue before any further special dividends.

companies.name: The North West Company
companies.banners: Northern, NorthMart, Giant Tiger, Alaska Commercial, Cost-U-Less, RiteWay
notes: Serves remote northern communities where it is often the only store, which supports steady margins.
Founding year reflects the Hudson's Bay Company trading posts the business descends from.

stores.basis: Northern Canada, Alaska, South Pacific, Caribbean

intl.evidence: Rural Alaska, South Pacific and Caribbean stores

logistics.evidence: Owns North Star Air cargo airline serving northern stores

health.evidence: Pharmacy and health services in remote communities

log.action: New store opened in Hagåtña, Guam
Bought a Basler BT-67 aircraft to replace leased planes
Next 100 program: assortment, procurement, private label
Labour productivity named a key H2 focus

actions: Capture the multi-year First Nations settlement spending with staples and big-ticket goods.
Owning aircraft lowers freight cost; tie fleet purchases to measured cost per kilogram.
Labour productivity is the stated gap; set and publish a target.

companies.name: Roots
notes: Agreed to be taken private by Marquee Brands at $4.10 a share; shareholders vote Oct 13, 2026. The price is pinned just under the offer.
Near-zero net income makes its P/E meaningless.

franchise.evidence: Partner and other revenue $9M in Q2

log.action: Agreed sale to Marquee Brands at $4.10 a share
Whistler flagship relocated after temporary closure

actions: The $4.10 offer caps the share price; the vote on Oct 13 decides everything else.
Under a brand-management owner, expect licensing and partner revenue to grow faster than owned stores.

companies.name: Groupe Dynamite
notes: Listed on the TSX in November 2024, so there is no 5-year beta.
Q2 (to Aug 1, 2026) revenue rose 29.8% with comparable sales up 10.3%; the trailing figures here stop one quarter earlier.
Pays a regular dividend: C$252M went to shareholders over the trailing twelve months.
companies.guidance: Company outlook: revenue growth raised to 25–27%

intl.evidence: Garage expanding in the U.S. (6 of 7 Q2 openings) and the UK

private.evidence: Two owned brands: Garage and Dynamite

log.action: 24–26 gross openings and 16 closures planned this year
First UK Garage open; Bullring store early 2027
Gross margin 68.8% on lower tariff and logistics costs

actions: Treat the UK as a test: expand only once those stores match U.S. productivity.
Keep closing weak Canadian stores while opening U.S. ones; the net count matters less than sales per store.
Growth is forecast to ease from 26% to 15%; hold marketing spend so the brand heat carries over.
